_comment: TWO B-roll cutaways plus four wipe transitions. broll_1 is this reel's own rendered motion-graphic stinger; matchcut is a user-supplied clip normalized into work/matchcut.mp4 by prep_matchcut.py. See broll.py for why segment 1 is the only place a MOTION-GRAPHIC cutaway belongs in this script, and the note below for why the supplied clip is the exception that earns segment 2.
_matchcut_note: The supplied newspaper text-match-cut ('JustAskEXPO' highlighted across successive article columns) goes at the top of segment 2, 6.60-8.10s, because that is where Tushar actually says 'At the Just Ask Expo' (Just 7.03, Ask 7.29, Expo 7.55-8.09) -- the highlighted words on screen land on the same words in the audio, which is the entire point of a match cut and the only placement where it is a match rather than a decoration. This is a deliberate exception to broll.py's rule that segment 2 is too information-dense to cover: that rule exists to stop graphics obscuring spoken facts, and here the graphic IS the fact being spoken. Only the first 1.5s of the 4.7s converted clip is used (see broll_durs); it is a continuous montage with no single climax, so the opening 'Breaking: JustAskEXPO' beat is as strong an entry as any later one.
_matchcut_length_note: Shortened 2.5s -> 1.5s on request. The window now covers 6.60-8.10s, which still spans the whole spoken campaign name ('Just' 7.03 through 'Expo' ending 8.09) -- so the match is intact and only the tail past the name was trimmed. Two knock-ons were handled rather than left stale: the return-to-camera whoosh moved 8.98 -> 7.98 to stay 0.12s ahead of the new 8.10 cut, and the expo poster was deliberately LEFT at its 9.45-11.91 slot. The poster could now technically move back to its original 25th-of-August anchor (7.91) since the match cut ends earlier, but that start still falls inside the 6.60-8.10 window, so it would reintroduce the poster-over-newspaper stack the re-anchor was done to remove. A happy side effect of the shorter cut: the 25 AUGUST highlight swipes in at 8.12, 0.02s after the return, so it lands exactly as the footage comes back -- and because this return is a plain cut with no wipe over it, nothing hides that entrance.
_placement_note: insert_broll.py splices B-roll into the START of a segment (out = broll[0:dur] + seg_video[dur:]), so a cutaway can only sit at a segment opening. boundaries are absolute times on the output timeline (cumulative segment durations 3.10 / 3.50 / 7.60 / 3.05 / 6.50 / 4.85 = 28.60).
_durs_note: broll_durs gives segment 2 a 2.5s splice while segment 1 keeps 1.0s. The reel-wide broll_dur could not express this -- it is one value for every planned segment -- so insert_broll.py gained an optional per-segment 'broll_durs' map (absent = previous behaviour exactly). 1.0s is right for broll_1 because the phrase it covers ends at 3.96s and the hero slam enters at 4.47s; 2.5s is what was asked for here and fits comfortably inside segment 2's 7.60s.
_wipes_note: Both B-roll boundaries now need a wipe, and those were previously hardcoded to the grid wipe -- which would have put grid at BOTH 3.10 and 6.60, the only two adjacent cuts in the reel. insert_broll.py gained an optional 'boundary_wipes' style map for this (absent = grid, as before), so 6.60 takes the diagonal speed sweep instead. Full sequence, no two adjacent alike: grid(3.10) -> speed(6.60) -> flash(14.20) -> grid(17.25) -> flash(23.75). 3.10 and 6.60 are NOT in extra_wipes any more -- boundaries already emits a wipe at each, and listing them twice would stack two wipes on the same frame.
